cards.text: Jonah son of Amittai got a job from the LORD: go to the great city of Nineveh. Instead he bought a ticket the OTHER way, a storm hit his ship, and the sailors threw him overboard. Now he's in the sea, and the sea just went calm, which is the most awkward kind of quiet there is.

cards.question: Jonah's been thrown into the sea, but the LORD already has a plan. What has the LORD appointed?

cards.text: And that great fish swallows Jonah. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even I'm looking at this going, "Okay, Jonah. YOU win."

cards.question: How long is Jonah in the belly of the fish?
Jonah is stuck inside the fish. What does he do from in there?

answers.text: He prays to the LORD his God
He falls into a deep sleep
He cries out to the sailors

cards.question: Jonah's prayer looks back on his distress. He says that when he called for help from the belly of Sheol, the LORD heard his voice.

cards.text: Then Jonah tells God about going under: the heart of the seas, the current swirling, and God's own breakers and waves sweeping over him. That's not a swim, friend, that's a SPIN CYCLE.

cards.question: In his prayer, who does Jonah say cast him into the deep?

cards.text: Jonah says it was the LORD who cast him in. Then he tells what he said in that moment: "I have been banished from Your sight"

cards.question: Jonah says he's been banished from God's sight. Does he give up on God?

answers.text: No he looks toward God's temple once more
Yes he stops calling out to God
Yes he hides himself from God for good

cards.text: Jonah keeps going: the waters engulf him, and the seaweed wraps around his head. I wear a tall chef's hat every single day, and friend, I have NEVER had a hat day that bad.

cards.question: Jonah says he sank to the roots of the mountains, and the earth barred him in forever. Then he says the LORD left his life down in the pit.
As his life was fading away, Jonah ___ the LORD.

cards.text: Then Jonah says his prayer went up to God, to His holy temple. Friend, that's the same temple he said he'd look toward once more, and his prayer made it ALL the way there.

cards.question: Near the end of his prayer, Jonah talks about people who cling to worthless idols. He says they hold on to God's loving devotion.

cards.text: But Jonah sets himself apart from them. He says he'll come to the LORD with the voice of thanksgiving.

cards.question: Jonah says he will ___ to the LORD and fulfill what he has ___.
Jonah ends his prayer by saying that ___ is from the LORD.
Jonah's prayer is done, and the LORD commands the fish. What does the fish do with Jonah?

answers.text: Spits him onto a passing ship
Carries him back out to sea

cards.text: The fish listens to the LORD, and I can't even get my own oven timer to listen to me. Trust me, friend, this story is far from done.

findings.problem: The card cites only Jonah 2:7, but its second sentence also retells Jonah 2:4 when it says Jonah had said he would look toward God's temple once more. The citation is narrower than the verses the card uses; following the first-to-last rule, it would be Jonah 2:4-7.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Neither card 16 nor the earlier setup establishes that Jonah will sacrifice or that he has made a vow. The baker must guess the unseen wording of Jonah 2:9, especially since both "sacrifice" and "bow" fit the first blank and "vowed," "planned," and "dreamed" can all fit the second.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
